title: Headroom budgeting for weights/KV/activations with continuous-batch-aware spill policies
creator: Ava Chen
body:
Summary:
We need a robust GPU memory budgeting strategy that divides and maintains headroom across weights, KV cache, and activations for continuous-batching workloads. This ticket explores a practical headroom split, a continuous-batch-aware spill/eviction policy (including host-spill), and a lightweight predictive hedging model to reduce OOMs and tail latencies during bursty tenant behavior. The goal is to keep OOMs near zero for production traffic while minimizing latency regressions and additional CPU/GPU transfer cost.

Background / Motivation:
- Continuous batching increases memory multiplexing efficiency but couples activation and KV pressure tightly with dynamic batch growth.
- Existing static watermarks frequently misallocate headroom (too conservative -> wasted throughput, too aggressive -> OOMs).
- We already have KV prefetch heuristics and soft-reserve lanes, but we lack a coordinated headroom accounting ledger that ties weights+KV+activations into a single budget with graceful degradation.

Objectives / Acceptance criteria:
- Design and prototype a headroom allocator that:
  * Enforces a soft split across weights, KV cache, and activations with configurable elasticity.
  * Supports continuous batching: headroom budgets should adapt within the request lifecycle (prefetch / decode / generate phases).
- Implement a host-spill fall-back for KV chunks and a prioritized eviction order that avoids dropping recently used activations.
- Add a predictive short-horizon hedging model (window=30s) for proactive KV pre-eviction when predicted headroom delta < threshold.
- Metrics/targets for rollout:
  * Production canary: OOM rate <= 0.0001 (1 per 10k requests)
  * Tail latency P95 increase <= 5% vs baseline
  * Eviction-induced request retries <= 0.5%

Proposed approach / Implementation plan:
1) Design: headroom ledger module
   - Maintain three tracked counters on each GPU: weights_resident, kv_resident, activation_resident.
   - Global GPU_mem_total = weights + kv + activations + headroom_reserved. Headroom_reserved acts as elastic buffer.
   - Introduce a soft-split config (example default: weights=0.60, kv=0.25, activations=0.15) with per-tenant scaling factor based on recent tail token length.
2) Continuous-batch integration
   - On request start: allocate activation budget estimate using token budget estimator (seq_len * per-token-activation).
   - During generation: periodically re-evaluate activation usage at batching boundaries; request dynamic bump from headroom if safe.
3) Spill and eviction policy
   - Primary: KV items are preferred for spill (least-recently-used with recency decay).
   - Secondary: host-spill buffer for compressed KV chunks (async cudaMemcpy to pinned host memory).
   - Avoid spilling weights. Activations are last-resort only when both KV and host-spill saturated.
4) Predictive hedging model
   - Lightweight exponential-smoothing model predicting short-term KV growth by tenant using last 30s windows of kv_alloc_rate and batch_arrival_rate.
   - If predicted headroom delta < X (configurable), proactively evict low-score KV shards or limit prefetch aggressiveness.
5) Telemetry & safety knobs
   - New metrics: gpu_mem_total, weights_resident, kv_resident, activation_resident, headroom_reserved, kv_eviction_count, host_spill_bytes, oom_events, request_retry_count, tail_latency_p95.
   - Safety thresholds and auto-breaker: if OOM_rate or tail_latency exceed thresholds, revert to conservative static headroom split and disable predictive hedging for that GPU.
6) Rollout plan
   - Canary: run on 1-2 canary GPUs serving low-traffic tenants for 48 hours.
   - Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 24h observation windows and rollback on SLO breach.

Experiments / Data we will collect:
- Synthetic stress tests: run mixtures of short chat and long-form generation to profile kv_alloc_rate and activation growth curves. Attach runbook links below.
- Replay production sampling: sample 10k requests per tenant to estimate per-tenant activation estimator accuracy.
- Cost analysis: measure extra CPU/mem bandwidth from host-spill and expected latency cost.

Open tradeoffs considered:
- Host-spill vs aggressive eviction: host-spill reduces OOM risk but increases latency and CPU usage; eviction keeps GPU hot set small but causes more cache misses and potential quality regression for repeated requests.
- Complex ML hedging model vs simple heuristic: we prefer a lightweight exponential-smoothing predictor to keep run-time cost small and to simplify correctness proofs for fail-open behavior.

Progress updates / timeline:
- 2026-03-02 Ava Chen: Initial design doc drafted. Linked design doc in Confluence (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRT/Headroom+Ledger+Design).
- 2026-03-04 Diego Ramirez: Prototype headroom ledger API sketched in runtime repo. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1823 (WIP).
- 2026-03-06 Priya Nandakumar: Ran synthetic replay test; found kv_eviction_count spiked when continuous-batch growth > 2x baseline. Attached perf traces: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kv-headroom/replay-run-20260306
- 2026-03-08 Review notes from Samir Patel (SRE): suggest adding per-GPU auto-breaker and explicit knob to disable host-spill under heavy PCIe utilization. Action: add metric pcie_util_percent and breaker threshold.
- 2026-03-09 Diego Ramirez: Implemented host-spill path and compressed-chunk format; initial microbench shows host-spill latency median = 12ms, P95 = 48ms for 4MB chunks. Linked PR update: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1823#issuecomment-4201

Tests and validation:
- Unit tests for ledger arithmetic and safe-concurrent updates.
- Integration tests with continuous-batcher simulator (added test scenario: multi-tenant bursts with 2-5x arriving batch scale).
- Load test plan: 4x synthetic concurrency for 6h to trigger sustained KV growth patterns.

Rollout & Monitoring checklist:
- Canary health dashboard (grafana panel id: kv-headroom-2026) with alerts for oom_rate > 0.0001 or tail_latency_p95 increase > 10% to be conservative during early rollout.
- Automated rollback script to flip feature flag and clear host-spill buffers if thresholds breached.

Open questions / next steps:
- Tunables: default soft-split numbers (weights/kv/activations) need A/B to pick production defaults. Propose A/B candidates: [0.60/0.25/0.15], [0.65/0.20/0.15], [0.55/0.30/0.15].
- How aggressive should predictive eviction be for high-priority (paid) tenants? Suggest per-tenant priority multiplier.
- Investigate compressed KV chunk format tradeoffs: compression ratio vs decompression CPU cost.

Links / artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRT/Headroom+Ledger+Design
- Runtime PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1823
- Perf dashboard (replay): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kv-headroom/replay-run-20260306
- Benchmarks notebook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Xy-example-notebook

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus reviews on the ledger arithmetic edge cases (concurrent reserve/release) and the safety breaker semantics.
- Security: host-spill stores compressed KV in pinned host memory; ensure KMS is not needed but we should confirm adherence to memory scrubbing policies — flagging security_review_required=false for now but will request review if host-spill touches persisted storage.

Next actions (owners):
- Diego: finish ledger concurrency guards and address Samir's breaker suggestion (3 days).
- Priya: expand synthetic replay coverage to include long-tail tenants and report recommended soft-split (4 days).
- Ava: draft rollout playbook and alert runbook for on-call (2 days).

Comments log:
- 2026-03-09 Samir Patel (SRE): "Add pcie_util_percent and a breaker. Host-spill is great but we must not saturate PCIe during peak backups."
- 2026-03-10 Priya Nandakumar: "Initial hedging model looks promising — reduces eviction spikes by ~35% in replay runs. We should tune smoothing alpha per-tenant."

Acceptance criteria checklist (to mark Done):
- [ ] Ledger module reviewed and merged
- [ ] Host-spill implemented with safety breaker
- [ ] Canary run >=48h within acceptance metrics
- [ ] Rollout playbook and rollback script completed
- [ ] Follow-up doc with chosen default soft-split and config published

If any of the acceptance metrics fail during canary, we will immediately revert to static headroom policy and open a postmortem ticket.
